reviews.rationale: The supplementary information describes simulations with bootstrapped non-uniform component errors showing Λ≈2 for distances up to 13, with small spread. This is directly supported.
The paper discusses dynamically created Z2 x Z2 symmetry, conservation of electric and magnetic charge, and materialized symmetry via unphysical degrees of freedom. Supported by p8 and p9.

The passage states that byproduct operators are not physically applied but tracked in the control software, as discussed in the section on software-implemented logical operators, directly supporting the applied_in relation.

The paper explicitly reports the distance-7 logical qubit lifetime of 291±6 µs, exceeding the best physical qubit lifetime (119±13 µs) by a factor of 2.4±0.3, and describes this as extending beyond break-even results from bosonic codes to multi-qubit codes. The metric definition is detailed in the supplementary information.

The claim accurately reflects the paper's reported results: a distance-7 surface code on a 105-qubit processor achieves ε7 = (1.43±0.03)×10^-3 (0.143%) and Λ=2.14±0.02, with simulations confirming below-threshold operation. The problem statement and conceptual move are consistent with the text.
The supplementary information describes estimating uncertainty in Λ by propagating uncertainties from individual code fits, accounting for drift-induced excess residuals. This is directly supported.

The paper and supplementary information state that scaling to 10^-6 error rate requires 1457 qubits with current performance, but halving physical error rates reduces this to 337 qubits, showing exponential leverage. This is directly supported.

The paper reports that activating DQLR increases Λ by 35% for distance-5, while detection probability decreases by only 12%, and states that addressing leakage is crucial for transmon surface codes. This is directly supported by the text.

The supplementary information defines effective lifetime as inverse depolarization rate from average channel fidelity, uniformly averaged over pure states, enabling comparison between physical and logical qubits. This is directly supported.

The paper states the Hamiltonian's ground state is 4-fold degenerate on a torus, degeneracy depends on genus, and local perturbations cause exponentially small splitting exp(-aL). Supported by p5 and p6.
The neural network decoder with gated recurrence is used to decode the distance-7 code up to 250 cycles, providing the reported Λ, directly supporting the relation.

The surface code is implemented on a 2D array where data qubits store computational states and measurement qubits (measure-Z and measure-X) stabilize neighboring data qubits via four-qubit operator products.
The surface code operates from a quiescent state randomly selected by completing one full cycle of stabilizer measurements, which is maintained in the absence of errors.

Single-qubit errors are detected by sign changes in adjacent stabilizer measurement outcomes: Z errors affect two neighboring measure-X qubits, X errors affect two measure-Z qubits, and Y errors affect both.
Logical operators XL and ZL are constructed as chains of single-qubit operators that cross the array, connecting boundaries of the same type, and anti-commute with each other.

A statistical model predicts the logical error rate by considering the most likely misidentifications between complementary error chains, yielding a scaling law PL ~ p^de.

The logical error rate is least sensitive to measure qubit errors (class-1), more sensitive to data qubit errors (class-0), and most sensitive to CNOT errors (class-2), with different thresholds for each class.
